glossary.definition: Directly measured by an attached telemetry source inside this incident's window. An observed statement is a fact about what a source recorded — not an interpretation.
Established by independent, agreeing evidence sources — never by one source repeating, and never by timing alone.
Supported by some evidence but not independently confirmed; alternative explanations remain open.

Evidence from measurement systems with no shared failure mode (for example an active check, a routing-plane event and a traffic measurement). Their agreement is information; one system repeating is not.
Effect on actual user traffic, shown only by evidence from real sessions or the serving infrastructure itself. It is a separate question from synthetic-check failures and is never derived from them.
No telemetry with valid provenance quantifies this value for this case. Not measured is stated as such — it is never rendered as zero, and it is not evidence of no impact.
An interval where a telemetry class produced no data. A gap is absence of measurement, not evidence of health — nothing is concluded from it.

summary.management: At 2026-11-12 04:50:50 UTC, automated telemetry detected a condition of “link state change” affecting the monitored service. A component recovered at 2026-11-12 04:54:36 UTC, but end-to-end service checks continued failing through 2026-11-12 04:54:41 UTC — the incident entered residual degradation rather than full recovery, and service recovery is not confirmed. The condition is ongoing (6m 24s elapsed). Customer impact could not be assessed — impact telemetry coverage was unavailable or insufficient for this window. The cause remains unconfirmed because independent evidence classes did not corroborate the observations. Decision: Hold — The evidence does not meet the ticket-open policy. Auto-ticketing holds until the policy threshold is met. Escalation follows the policy thresholds stated in the decision section.
